cards.text: Last time, Boaz, a relative of Naomi's (Ruth 2:1), told Ruth that if the nearer kinsman-redeemer won't redeem her, he will (Ruth 3:13). Naomi said Boaz won't rest until the matter is settled today (Ruth 3:18). Meanwhile, Boaz goes to the city gate and sits down.

cards.question: Boaz is sitting at the city gate. Who comes walking along?

answers.text: One of the young men from the field

cards.text: Boaz calls out, "Come over here, my friend, and sit down." So he sits, and I bet he has NO idea what kind of day he's about to have.

cards.question: Next, Boaz gathers ___ of the elders of the city and tells them to sit down too.

cards.text: Then Boaz gets down to business. Naomi, who has come back from Moab, is selling the land that belonged to Elimelech, her late husband (Ruth 1:3).
Boaz says he's telling the man first, right in front of the elders. If you want to redeem it, do so, and if not, say so.

cards.question: Boaz tells the man that Boaz himself is first in line to redeem Elimelech's land, ahead of him.
Boaz asks the nearer kinsman-redeemer whether he wants to redeem Elimelech's land. What does the man say?

cards.text: HA, that man said yes like somebody just yelled FREE COOKIES. But Boaz isn't done talking.

cards.question: Boaz adds a catch. On the day the man buys the land from Naomi and Ruth the Moabitess, what else must he do?

answers.text: Acquire the widow of the deceased
Pay the debts of the deceased
Repair the house of the deceased

cards.text: Whoa, the land deal just came with a wedding attached. That's like grabbing ONE free sample and finding out you just agreed to run the whole bakery.

cards.question: Now that Ruth is part of the deal, the nearer kinsman-redeemer still wants to redeem the land.
The nearer kinsman-redeemer says he cannot redeem it after all. What reason does he give?

answers.text: It would jeopardize his own inheritance
He can't afford the price Naomi is asking
He already has too many fields to work

cards.text: He tells Boaz, "Take my right of redemption, because I cannot redeem it." And just like that, the door swings wide open for Boaz.
Quick note on how deals worked back then. In former times in Israel, a deal about redeeming or trading property was made legally binding with one simple move.

cards.question: To make a property deal binding in Israel, a man would remove his ___ and give it to the other party.

cards.text: So the man pulls off his sandal and says to Boaz, "Buy it for yourself." No pens, no fine print, just one shoe changing hands.

cards.question: Boaz tells the elders and all the people they are witnesses that he is buying from Naomi everything that belonged to Elimelech and his sons Chilion and Mahlon (Ruth 1:2).

cards.text: Then Boaz announces he has acquired Ruth the Moabitess, Mahlon's widow, as his wife.

cards.question: Boaz says he's taking Ruth as his wife so that something of the deceased won't disappear from among his brothers. What is it?

cards.text: Back at the city gate, the elders and all the people answer Boaz, "We are witnesses," and they're not done talking.

cards.question: The people at the gate say, May the LORD make the woman entering Boaz's home like two women who together built up the house of Israel. Which two?

cards.text: Rachel and Leah were the wives of Jacob (Genesis 29:30). Then the crowd says, "May you be prosperous in Ephrathah and famous in Bethlehem," and friend, the closest I ever got to famous was the back of a junk drawer, with a fan club of one twist tie.

cards.question: The crowd also says, may Boaz's house become like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, one of Jacob's sons (Genesis 35:23). They say it's because of something the LORD will give Boaz by this young woman. What is it?

cards.text: So Boaz takes Ruth, and she becomes his wife. From gleaning behind his harvesters (Ruth 2:3) to married to the boss, talk about a promotion.

cards.question: After Ruth becomes Boaz's wife, the LORD enables her to conceive, and she gives birth to a son.

cards.text: Then the women speak to Naomi. Remember, this is the woman who came home telling them to call her Mara, because the Almighty had dealt bitterly with her (Ruth 1:20).

cards.question: The women say to Naomi, Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you this day without what?
The women tell Naomi her daughter-in-law, who loves her, is better to her than seven sons. They mean Ruth has blessed Naomi more than many sons could.

cards.text: SEVEN sons, not one, not two, SEVEN, and Ruth still comes out on top. That's the greatest daughter-in-law review I've ever heard.

cards.question: Naomi takes the child, places him on her lap, and becomes a nurse to him.

cards.text: The woman who said the LORD brought her back empty (Ruth 1:21) now has a baby on her lap.

cards.question: Boaz and Ruth are the ones who name the baby.

cards.text: It's the neighbor women who do the naming. They say, "A son has been born to Naomi," and there it is, Naomi's name on it, not Ruth's.

cards.question: The neighbor women name the baby ___.
Obed becomes the father of Jesse. And Jesse becomes the father of which famous man?

cards.text: DAVID. The woman from Moab who followed Naomi home (Ruth 1:16) is the great-grandmother of David, who would become king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3).
The book ends with the family line of Perez, the same Perez from the blessing at the gate. Ten names, father to son, from Perez down to David, and right there in the line is Boaz, the father of Obed.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the number of elders, but nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out ten rather than seven or twelve. It can only be guessed from an unseen detail.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup says only that one simple move made a property deal binding. It gives no basis for reasoning out sandal rather than ring or cloak, so the blank depends on luck.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The baby's name has not been hinted at, and the three similar names give the baker no way to reason toward Obed. The blank is therefore a guess at an unseen detail.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
